decisions.chrome: the document draws the map, the search, the readout that changes and the picked-item box; the census, the kinds, the chips, the layout choice and the download controls are published on window.__bbView and drawn by the one sidebar
decisions.language: the language of a file is the projection's own field (group), with `language` honoured only as a fallback, so the grouping, the legend and the picked-item box cannot name two different languages for one symbol
decisions.filters: a filtered band is MUTED rather than removed: a treemap's areas ARE the line spans, so removing one would leave a hole where code demonstrably is. Muted bands stay counted, searchable and in the data port
decisions.budget: both cuts — the noise filter's exclusions and the node budget's — are rows in the census rather than discoveries
decisions.lod: a file whose every stripe would fall under MIN_STRIPE_PX at the zoom being drawn is drawn as ONE composition strip, as tall as its cell, whose slices are the lines each kind spans AND the code between them in source order — so the area contract and the muted tone survive the fold, and the count is published rather than implied
decisions.readability: readability is judged by a symbol's HONEST share of its cell (span / the file's lines), never by the floored height it is drawn at: the floor is a drawing device, and judging by it made the answer depend on the cell's shape rather than the file's density
decisions.labels: a name is printed only when it fits WHOLE — measured with a canvas where one exists, with a documented per-character fallback under the stub — largest area first, each kind capped at half the budget, and a stripe that starts under its cell's header moves its name down instead of losing it
decisions.concentration: the census names the share of drawn area held by the largest 20 symbols when it is 25% or more, because a reader looking at a one-colour picture is owed the reason: over src/ the answer is that 93.7% of the spanned lines in scope are functions and methods, and one method spans 3,500 of its file's 6,183 lines
decisions.layout: the file layout divides by the file's LAST LINE and positions by absolute line numbers; before this pass it divided by the sum of the symbols' spans while positioning by line numbers, so 8 of 92 files over src/ drew more content than their cell could hold (real-cpp-analyzer.ts drew 7,760 units into 3,513) and every gap band was painted under the band that followed it
decisions.stub: the gate executes the emitted script against a stub DOM resolved from the document's own markup: an id the document no longer carries resolves to null, so a regression that paints into a removed panel fails loudly

limitations: The stub DOM is not a browser: layout is not computed (a rect is parsed from the element's own inline style), so this gate proves what the artifact PUBLISHES and DRAWS DECLARES, not where the pixels land. The pixels are V10's job (script/m13/verify-visualize-browser.ts, run as `npm run verify:viz-browser`).

One fixture (2 TypeScript files, 1 Python file, 1 vendored path) plus two hand-built payloads for the cases a fixture cannot produce: a symbol whose `group` and `language` disagree, and a node budget that cuts.

The screenshot evidence for the composed sidebar of the graph view lives in validation/m13/results/viz-layout-panel; the code map's own composed page is asserted structurally here and its document behaviourally.

OUT OF SCOPE, named here because a fixture hit it: squarify's row placement can give one file a cell TALLER than the world it is laid into (measured with two files whose line counts are 30:1 apart: a 62x1,951px cell inside a 1,220px world), so content can hang below the frame. The density assertions therefore use a twelve-file fixture and a 900x600 viewport, where the same payload reproduces the density a reader complains about instead of an artefact of the row placement.

The pixels are still not read here: this gate proves what the artifact DRAWS and PUBLISHES (element counts, gradients, label boxes from inline styles), not where they land. Label clipping measured on screen, and the zoom-settle redraw, belong to V10 (script/m13/verify-visualize-browser.ts).
